root_cause_criterion.criterion: After `UA_Array_delete((void*)(uintptr_t)ac->userTokenPolicies, ac->userTokenPoliciesSize, ...)` frees the array during the first cleanup, `deleteMembers_default()` must reset `ac->userTokenPoliciesSize` to 0 before any later cleanup revisits the same `UA_AccessControl`. Otherwise the second cleanup still iterates two `UA_UserTokenPolicy` elements and re-enters generic clear on freed storage.
root_cause_criterion.description: The selected root obligation is that the first cleanup must clear the stale policy count immediately after freeing the `userTokenPolicies` array. The vulnerable first cleanup leaves `ac->userTokenPoliciesSize` at 2, so a later `UA_Server_delete()` cleanup can still walk freed `UA_UserTokenPolicy` elements.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: Not runtime-verified on the authoritative fixed original case: the `-fix` image stays clean but does not execute `first_policy_free_post`, so the frozen required assertion remains `not_exercised` there.

nodes.state: `String_clear()` is reached with `s` still equal to the freed `UA_UserTokenPolicy` array base (the first `policyId` string subobject), so the immediately following `s->data` load is the AddressSanitizer-reported heap-use-after-free read.

edges.relation: The same array-base pointer left in `ac->userTokenPolicies` after the first free is later reused by the second cleanup and arrives at `String_clear()` as its `s` argument when clearing the first `policyId` string, so the free happens before the stale use on that exact address.
